newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill Lynch sees slower Q2 for Warsaw bourse.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch sees slower Q2 for Warsaw bourse.

text.p: Merrill Lynch in London sees a slower second quarter for the Warsaw bourse with several big public offerings and the listing of National Investment Funds (NFIs) drawing attention from listed shares, Merrill said.

"The listing of the (NFIs) by the end of the second quarter is likely to divert much of investors' attention from the current listed companies," Merrill said in its quarterly European Emerging Markets strategy report dated April 4.
The Warsaw bourse closed at 16,634.9 points on Monday, compared with the end-1996 level of 14,342.8.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.

"Differentiation will be key to the funds' ability to attract international investors and some (NFIs') plans to promote transparency should yield significant initial increases in NAVs," the report added.
Merrill also said uncertainty about the outcome of the parliamentary elections due in September was another reason for the expected slowing in the second quarter.
It also said company earnings were suffering from accelerating depreciation charges caused by heavy investment, as well as increasing foreign competition.

"Following a 22 percent increase in share prices in the first two months of the year, valuations began to appear unwarranted particularly against the backdrop of single digit real earnings growth," Merrill said.
